title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 404
paragraphs: In what way, then, one will ask, are they used up? This also I will explain. The head-man of each place must collect all the earthenware jars from his own town and convey them to Memphis, and those at Memphis must fill them with water and carry them to these same waterless regions of Syria. So the jars, which come regularly to Egypt and are emptied there, are carried off to Syria to be added to those that have come before. It was the Persians who thus prepared this approach to Egypt, supplying it with water in the manner described, from the time when they first took possession of Egypt. But at the time I speak of, since water was not yet provided, Cambyses, acting on the advice of his Halicarnassian guest, sent envoys to the Arabian king and asked from him — and obtained — safe passage, having given him pledges of friendship and received them from him in return.
